data.narrative:
GITAI is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $129M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of nine private robotics peers at similar or adjacent stages (Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and others) plus one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yields $219M. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector comparables at matching or proximate stages produces a $1.6B median valuation, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer set includes Exotec at $2.0B (Series D), Generalist AI at $2.0B (Series B), Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), and Hadrian at $1.6B (Series D).

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: low of $186M, median of $935M, and high of $1.9B. The stage-progression method suggests conservative valuation near the lower bound, while peer comparison supports the $1.6B median or higher. The wide spread reflects uncertainty around GITAI's relative positioning within the robotics sector—specifically, whether it commands premium or discount multiples relative to named peers, and the degree to which stage-adjacent comparables remain relevant. Revenue traction, unit economics, and competitive moat clarity would narrow this range materially.
